claim: Cephalopods are set apart from other mollusks by their advanced behavioral abilities and the complexity of their nervous systems.
source: Cephalopods are set apart from other mollusks by their advanced behavioral abilities and the complexity of their nervous systems.
evidence: This is a general statement about cephalopods that draws from established scientific knowledge about their unique characteristics among mollusks.

claim: Higher cognitive features have evolved separately in cephalopods and vertebrates despite the similarities that they share.
source: Because of the great evolutionary distance that separates vertebrates from cephalopods, it is evident that higher cognitive features have evolved separately in these clades despite the similarities that they share.
evidence: This statement is based on established evolutionary knowledge about the phylogenetic distance between cephalopods and vertebrates and the concept of convergent evolution.

claim: Cephalopods have evolved specialized cells and tissues, such as chromatophores for camouflage or suckers to grasp prey.
source: Alongside their complex behavioral abilities, cephalopods have evolved specialized cells and tissues, such as the chromatophores for camouflage or suckers to grasp prey.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about cephalopod anatomy and function.

claim: The molecular identities of cell types in cephalopods remain largely unknown despite significant progress in genome and transcriptome sequencing.
source: Despite significant progress in genome and transcriptome sequencing, the molecular identities of cell types in cephalopods remain largely unknown.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of knowledge in the field and provides context for the study.

claim: The study combines single-cell transcriptomics with in situ gene expression analysis to uncover cell type diversity in the European squid Loligo vulgaris.
source: We here combine single-cell transcriptomics with in situ gene expression analysis to uncover cell type diversity in the European squid Loligo vulgaris.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach of the study.

claim: The study describes cell types that are conserved with other phyla such as neurons, muscles, or connective tissues.
source: We describe cell types that are conserved with other phyla such as neurons, muscles, or connective tissues but also cephalopod-specific cells, such as chromatophores or sucker cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: The study describes cephalopod-specific cells, such as chromatophores or sucker cells.
source: We describe cell types that are conserved with other phyla such as neurons, muscles, or connective tissues but also cephalopod-specific cells, such as chromatophores or sucker cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: The study investigates major components of the squid nervous system including progenitor and developing cells, differentiated cells of the brain and optic lobes, as well as sensory systems of the head.
source: Moreover, we investigate major components of the squid nervous system including progenitor and developing cells, differentiated cells of the brain and optic lobes, as well as sensory systems of the head.
evidence: This describes the scope of the study's investigation of the nervous system.

claim: Cephalopods possess a sophisticated nervous system that resembles that of vertebrates in relative size and cognitive abilities.
source: Cephalopods possess a sophisticated nervous system that resembles that of vertebrates in relative size and cognitive abilities (Young, 1991; Hochner et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Cephalopods exhibit complex behavioral abilities including various forms of learning, problem-solving, and body color and pattern changes used for predatory or anti-predatory behaviors or for social communication.
source: These complex behavioral abilities include various forms of learning, problem-solving, and body color and pattern changes used either as predatory or anti-predatory behaviors or for social communication (Fiorito et al., 1990; Langridge et al., 2007; Staudinger et al., 2013; Darmaillacq et al., 2014; Schnell et al., 2015; Richter et al., 2016; Lin and Chiao, 2017; Marini et al., 2017; Mather and Dickel, 2017; Hanlon and Messenger, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: The fossil record suggests that cephalopods were more prominent in marine ecosystems over 300 million years ago with a higher biodiversity than today.
source: The fossil record suggests that cephalopods were more prominent in marine ecosystems over 300 million years ago with a higher biodiversity than today.
evidence: This is based on paleontological knowledge from the fossil record.

claim: The rise of bony fishes and resulting competition for resources played a major role in the extinction of many clades of cephalopods.
source: It is assumed that the rise of bony fishes and resulting competition for resources in that ecological niche played a major role in the extinction of many clades of cephalopods, including all the shelled cephalopods except few members of the subclass Nautiloidea.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about cephalopod evolution based on ecological and evolutionary reasoning.

claim: The class Cephalopoda has over 800 current living species with extremely diversified lifestyles and body shapes.
source: Today, the class Cephalopoda has over 800 current living species with extremely diversified lifestyles and body shapes (Kröger et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a factual statement about cephalopod diversity supported by a citation.

claim: The vast majority of current cephalopod species belong to the soft-bodied subclass Coleoidea.
source: The vast majority of current cephalopod species belong to the soft-bodied subclass Coleoidea (cuttlefishes, octopuses, and squids), and a small handful belong to the subclass Nautiloidea (nautiluses).
evidence: This is a factual statement about cephalopod taxonomy based on established knowledge.

claim: Coleoid cephalopods have internalized or lost their shell over evolutionary time.
source: Coleoid cephalopods, which have internalized or lost their shell over evolutionary time, were able to swim more easily and could compete with other predators in open waters.
evidence: This is a statement about cephalopod evolution based on established knowledge.

claim: Continuous competition with other animals to access resources has been proposed to have been the main trigger for the selection of cephalopods that could develop specialized strategies.
source: The continuous competition with other animals to access resources has been proposed to have been the main trigger for the selection of cephalopods that could develop specialized strategies for accessing resources unavailable to competing species.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about evolutionary pressures on cephalopods.

claim: In coleoid cephalopods, evolutionary processes resulted in larger brains, camera-type eyes, and abilities to voluntarily change their skin pattern and texture for camouflage and social communication.
source: In coleoid cephalopods, this evolutionary process resulted in larger brains, camera-type eyes, as well as abilities to voluntarily change their skin pattern and texture for camouflage and social communication (Young, 1973; Hanlon and Messenger, 2018; Amodio et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The European squid Loligo vulgaris is well known for its economic role in the food and fishing industry.
source: The European squid Loligo vulgaris is well known for its economic role in the food and fishing industry but is much less studied for its fascinating biology.
evidence: This is a statement about the economic importance of L. vulgaris based on general knowledge.

claim: Loligo vulgaris is known for its striking ability for camouflage typically in open-water environments by the use of its specialized iridescent cells to reflect light in different manners depending on its surroundings.
source: This species is known for its striking ability for camouflage typically in open-water environments by the use of its specialized iridescent cells to reflect light in different manners depending on its surroundings.
evidence: This is a statement about the camouflage abilities of L. vulgaris based on established knowledge.

claim: The neuroanatomy and nervous system morphology of L. vulgaris have been described in detail in histological studies.
source: The neuroanatomy and nervous system morphology of L. vulgaris have been described in detail in histological studies (Young, 1976; Wild et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Detailed staging of the embryonic development of the related species Loligo pealii was established and can be used as a reference for L. vulgaris.
source: Detailed staging of the embryonic development of the related species Loligo pealii was established and can be used as a reference for L. vulgaris (Arnold, 1965).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: We are currently lacking resolution at the molecular level to identify genes that specify the many cell types that make up the unique cephalopod body-plan and nervous system.
source: While the gross anatomy of squids is well known from histology and morphological studies, we are currently lacking resolution at the molecular level to identify genes that specify the many cell types that make up the unique cephalopod body-plan and nervous system.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of knowledge in the field and provides context for the study.

claim: The first complete genome sequence of Octopus bimaculoides has been published.
source: Since the publication of the first complete genome sequence of Octopus bimaculoides, there has been increasing interest in cephalopod biology and neuroscience.
evidence: This is a factual statement about a published genome sequence.

claim: Genomic sequences are available for Euprymna scolopes (Sepiida), Architeuthis dux (Oegopsida), and Nautilus pompilius (Nautilida).
source: In addition, the availability of genomic sequences of other cephalopods, such as Euprymna scolopes (Sepiida), Architeuthis dux (Oegopsida), and Nautilus pompilius (Nautilida), opens the possibility for molecular comparisons between these distant clades of cephalopods with drastically different morphologies and lifestyles.
evidence: This is a factual statement about available genomic resources.

claim: Molecular comparisons between distant clades of cephalopods constitute a major step for understanding the molecular basis of cephalopod evolution.
source: These comparisons constitute a major step for understanding the molecular basis of cephalopod evolution (Albertin et al., 2015; Belcaid et al., 2019; da Fonseca et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Single-cell transcriptomics experiments in different cephalopods have shed light on the cell type diversity of the O. bimaculoides visual system, the brain of Octopus vulgaris, and the nervous system of the squid Euprymna berryi.
source: Single-cell transcriptomics experiments in different cephalopods have shed light on the cell type diversity of the O. bimaculoides visual system, the brain of Octopus vulgaris, and the nervous system of the squid Euprymna berryi (Gavriouchkina et al., 2022; Songco-Casey et al., 2022; Styfhals et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Single-cell transcriptomics was performed on whole L. vulgaris heads at stages 28–30 (pre-hatchling stage).
source: To gain further insights into the cellular diversity and cell type-specific gene expression in squids, we performed single-cell transcriptomics on whole L. vulgaris heads (stages 28–30 based on Arnold, 1965, pre-hatchling stage).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach of the study.

claim: Hybridization chain reaction in situ hybridization (HCR ISH) was used to visualize gene expression in situ and correlate single-cell transcriptomes with anatomical features.
source: Additionally, we used hybridization chain reaction in situ hybridization (HCR ISH) to visualize gene expression in situ and correlate single-cell transcriptomes with anatomical features.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach of the study.

claim: Common cell types found in most bilaterians, such as different types of neurons, muscles, and connective tissues, were identified and assessed.
source: By combining these methods, we were able to identify and assess common cell types found in most bilaterians, such as different types of neurons, muscles, and connective tissues.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Certain clusters of connective tissues highly express cephalopod-specific genes.
source: Interestingly, even in these canonical tissues, we found certain clusters that highly express cephalopod-specific genes, as exemplified by some subtypes of connective tissues.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: While cells can be assigned a certain identity based on well-characterized marker genes, such as collagens, these cell types have likely further diverged in cephalopods.
source: Thus, while cells can be assigned a certain identity based on well-characterized marker genes, such as collagens, these cell types have likely further diverged in cephalopods.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data suggesting evolutionary divergence.

claim: Neural tissues in the head include the brain, optic ganglia, eyes, and other sensory organs.
source: Neural tissues are prominent in the head and include the brain, optic ganglia, eyes, and other sensory organs.
evidence: This is a statement about the anatomical composition of the head based on established knowledge.

claim: New markers of different cells in the nervous system were identified and analyzed, including widely expressed pan-neuronal genes, genes marking distinct stages of neural differentiation, markers for neural subsets, as well as sensory cell types.
source: We identified and analyzed new markers of different cells in the nervous system, including widely expressed pan-neuronal genes, genes marking distinct stages of neural differentiation, markers for neural subsets, as well as sensory cell types.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Cephalopod-specific cell types, such as the chromatophores or cells of the suckers, were characterized.
source: In addition, we also characterized cephalopod-specific cell types, such as the chromatophores or cells of the suckers.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: A reference transcriptome of L. vulgaris was generated from embryos collected at late embryonic stages.
source: To generate a reference transcriptome of L. vulgaris, embryos were collected at late embryonic stages for RNA extraction and subsequent cDNA synthesis. The transcriptome was sequenced, assembled de novo, and annotated (for details, see 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This describes the experimental approach of the study.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed from the dissociated cells of the whole heads of L. vulgaris pre-hatchlings.
source: Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed from the dissociated cells of the whole heads of L. vulgaris pre-hatchlings.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach of the study.

claim: The mapping rate of the sequences was 29.3% and 29.8% for samples 1 and 2, respectively.
source: The mapping rate of the sequences was of 29.3% and 29.8% for samples 1 and 2, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sequencing analysis shown in the figure.

claim: The low mapping rate can be explained by L. vulgaris genes not being mapped to the transcriptome because the genes are missing from the transcriptome and by the presence of cells and ambient RNA from other species in the single-cell suspension.
source: This low mapping rate can be explained by L. vulgaris genes not being mapped to the transcriptome because the genes are missing from the transcriptome and by the presence of cells and ambient RNA from other species in the single-cell suspension.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the low mapping rate based on technical considerations.

claim: The assessment of the transcriptome assembly using BUSCO showed a score of 54.4% (49.8% single-copy, 4.6% duplicated, 1.9% fragmented).
source: The assessment of the transcriptome assembly using benchmark universal single-copy orthologs (BUSCO) showed a score of 54.4% (49.8% single-copy, 4.6% duplicated, 1.9% fragmented), which indicates that a number of genes are likely missing from our transcriptome that in turn may impact downstream analysis.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the transcriptome quality assessment.

claim: A number of genes are likely missing from the transcriptome which may impact downstream analysis.
source: The assessment of the transcriptome assembly using benchmark universal single-copy orthologs (BUSCO) showed a score of 54.4% (49.8% single-copy, 4.6% duplicated, 1.9% fragmented), which indicates that a number of genes are likely missing from our transcriptome that in turn may impact downstream analysis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the BUSCO score.

claim: 20,000 cells were analyzed in the study.
source: 20,000 cells were analyzed in our study.
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about the number of cells analyzed.

claim: Cells were filtered to keep only the ones with a gene-per-cell count comprised between 200 and 2000 (median = 700 genes/cell).
source: Cells were filtered to keep only the ones with a gene-per-cell count comprised between 200 and 2000 (median = 700 genes/cell).
evidence: This describes the data filtering approach.

claim: The filtering step resulted in a total of 19,974 cells.
source: This filtering step resulted in a total of 19,974 cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data filtering.

claim: Clustering was performed with Seurat using 25 principal components with a resolution value of 2.
source: Clustering was performed with Seurat using 25 principal components with a resolution value of 2.
evidence: This describes the computational analysis approach.

claim: Clustering resulted in a total of 34 cell clusters numbered from 0 to 33.
source: This resulted in a total of 34 cell clusters numbered from 0 to 33.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the clustering analysis.

claim: Clusters were assigned to presumed cell type identities based on the genes differentially expressed in each cluster.
source: Clusters were assigned to presumed cell type identities based on the genes differentially expressed in each cluster (Cl).
evidence: This describes the approach for assigning cell type identities.

claim: Defined cell type categories include muscle, connective tissue, stem cells, epidermis, papilin+ cells, neurons, foxD1+ cells, reflectin+ cells, ASc+ cells, cilia-related cells, photoreceptors, sucker, and lens.
source: These defined cell type categories include muscle, connective tissue, stem cells, epidermis, papilin+ cells, neurons, foxD1+ cells, reflectin+ cells, ASc+ cells, cilia-related cells, photoreceptors, sucker, and lens.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Muscle cells are identified based on the expression of various genes involved in the formation of contractile fibers such as myosin heavy chain, troponin, myosin regulatory light chain, paramyosin, tropomysin (Cl00).
source: The identification of muscle cells is based on the expression of various genes involved in the formation of contractile fibers such as myosin heavy chain, troponin, myosin regulatory light chain, paramyosin, tropomysin (Cl00).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: A second muscle cluster (Cl25) expresses markers including myosin catalytic light chain and paramyosin but is also distinguished by the expression of the transcription factor soxE.
source: A second muscle cluster (Cl25) expresses markers including myosin catalytic light chain and paramyosin but is also distinguished by the expression of the transcription factor soxE.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Smooth muscle-like cells (Cl25) are characterized by the expression of the homeobox transcription factor nkx2-5 and angiopoietin-1 receptor.
source: Smooth muscle-like cells (Cl25) are characterized by the expression of the homeobox transcription factor nkx2-5, which plays a crucial role in cardiac development in human embryos and angiopoietin-1 receptor, involved in angiogenesis in many species (Elliott et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, with supporting citation.

claim: Smooth muscle-like cells could be a part of the squid circulatory system.
source: Because of the presence of these two markers, we hypothesize that these cells could be a part of the squid circulatory system.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the expression of specific markers.

claim: Connective tissues are defined by the very broad expression of many different types of collagens (Cl01, Cl06, Cl23, Cl28).
source: Connective tissues are defined by the very broad expression of many different types of collagens, which are one of the main components of connective tissues (Cl01, Cl06, Cl23, Cl28).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: The presence of enriched laminin and fibroblast growth factor receptor suggests that connective tissue clusters include precursors or differentiated cells of connective tissues.
source: The presence of enriched laminin and fibroblast growth factor receptor further suggests that these cell clusters include precursors or differentiated cells of connective tissues.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on marker expression.

claim: Connective tissue markers are co-expressed with several uncharacterized genes that have known orthologs in other cephalopod species.
source: These markers that are typical of connective tissues are, however, co-expressed with several uncharacterized genes that have known orthologs in other cephalopod species.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Cells of the epidermis are characterized based on the expression of an egf-like epidermal growth factor (Cl08, Cl09).
source: Cells of the epidermis are characterized based on the expression of an egf-like epidermal growth factor (Cl08, Cl09).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Cl08 comprises chromatophores defined by the co-expression of tyrosinase and tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase, two members of the melanin synthesis pathway.
source: Interestingly, Cl08 comprises chromatophores defined by the co-expression of tyrosinase and tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase, two members of the melanin synthesis pathway that, when knocked out, have been shown to result in depigmentation in Doryteuthis pealeii (Crawford et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, with supporting citation.

claim: Cl31 was characterized by a different epithelial marker epithelial splicing regulatory protein (esrp).
source: Cl31 was characterized by a different epithelial marker epithelial splicing regulatory protein (esrp).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Three clusters (Cl03, Cl04, Cl12) highly express papilin, a gene which was suggested to play a role in the formation of extracellular matrix in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: Three clusters (Cl03, Cl04, Cl12) highly express papilin, a gene which was suggested to play a role in the formation of extracellular matrix in Drosophila melanogaster (Fessler et al., 2004; Apte, 2020).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, with supporting citations.

claim: Cells of the suckers (Cl29) could be identified by the enriched expression of suckerin genes that have been shown to be expressed in the sucker ring teeth of squids.
source: Cells of the suckers (Cl29) could be identified by the enriched expression of suckerin genes that have been shown to be expressed in the sucker ring teeth of squids (Kumar et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, with supporting citation.

claim: Neurons were identified based on widely used markers, including two genes belonging to the ELAV RNA-binding protein family elav-like 1 and elav-like 2 (Cl05, Cl07, Cl11, Cl13, Cl15).
source: Neurons were identified based on widely used markers, including two genes belonging to the ELAV RNA-binding protein family elav-like 1 and elav-like 2 (Cl05, Cl07, Cl11, Cl13, Cl15).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Known markers for the presynaptic machinery such as synaptobrevin, synaptogyrin, synaptophysin, and synapse-associated protein 1 are broadly expressed in neuronal clusters.
source: Known markers for the presynaptic machinery such as synaptobrevin, synaptogyrin, synaptophysin, and synapse-associated protein 1 are also broadly expressed in these clusters as well as amyloid beta-binding-like, tetraspanin-8, and rab3.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Cl27 is characterized by the expression of different cilia-related and flagella-related markers, together with the neuronal gene rab3 and synaptogyrin-1.
source: Cl27 is characterized by the expression of different cilia-related and flagella-related markers, together with the neuronal gene rab3 and synaptogyrin-1.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: The presence of cilia/flagella-related genes together with neuronal markers in Cl27 could suggest a mechanosensory function.
source: The modality of these cells remains unknown, but the presence of cilia/flagella-related genes together with neuronal markers could suggest a mechanosensory function (see Figure 4).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the expression of specific markers.

claim: Photoreceptors (Cl32) could be identified based on the expression of various members of the canonical phototransduction cascade, including trp-like, visual arrestin, retinal binding protein, phospholipase C, and rhodopsin.
source: Photoreceptors (Cl32) could be identified based on the expression of various members of the canonical phototransduction cascade, including trp-like, visual arrestin, retinal binding protein, phospholipase C, and rhodopsin.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Cl16, Cl19, and Cl30 are very clearly defined by the expression of the forkhead box transcription factor foxD1.
source: Cl16, Cl19, and Cl30 are very clearly defined by the expression of the forkhead box transcription factor foxD1.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: A large proportion of foxD+ cells co-express the transcription factor ets4.
source: A large proportion of these cells co-express the transcription factor ets4.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: In Cl30, foxD1 was co-expressed with a GATA zinc-finger protein (gata-2) and a few blood-related markers (ferritin, hemocyte, apolipophorin).
source: In Cl30, foxD1 was co-expressed with a GATA zinc-finger protein (gata-2) and a few blood-related markers (ferritin, hemocyte, apolipophorin).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Cl20 and Cl22 are characterized by the expression of different types of reflectin genes, a family of proteins used in cephalopods to control light reflection by modulating the iridescence of the skin.
source: Cl20 and Cl22 are characterized by the expression of different types of reflectin genes, a family of proteins used in cephalopods to control light reflection by modulating the iridescence of the skin (Crookes et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, with supporting citation.

claim: The transcriptional repressor scratch-2 is highly expressed in several neuronal clusters and in reflectin+ cells.
source: Interestingly, the transcriptional repressor scratch-2, which is highly expressed in several neuronal clusters, is also highly expressed in reflectin+ cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Expression of reflectins is observed in neurons.
source: We also observe expression of reflectins in neurons in agreement with this notion.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Different types of neural progenitors (Cl21, Cl26) are characterized by the high expression of a soxB1 and an achaete-scute (asc).
source: Different types of neural progenitors (Cl21, Cl26) are characterized by the high expression of a soxB1 and an achaete-scute (asc).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Genes of the achaete-scute complex have been broadly studied for their implication in the specification of the neuronal lineage, particularly in the fruit fly.
source: Genes of the achaete-scute complex have been broadly studied for their implication in the specification of the neuronal lineage, particularly in the fruit fly (Campuzano and Modolell, 1992; Skeath and Doe, 1996; Zhao et al., 2007; Arefin et al., 2019; Soares et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Neural progenitor clusters also express histone-related genes and markers of proliferation, suggesting that they may be replicating undifferentiated cells.
source: Both clusters also express histone-related genes and markers of proliferation, suggesting that they may be replicating undifferentiated cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on marker expression.

claim: The presence of a soxB1 in neural progenitor cells indicates that they may be proliferating neuronal progenitors, based on previous evidence of expression of soxB1 genes during neurogenesis in cephalopods.
source: The presence of a soxB1 in these cells indicates that they may be proliferating neuronal progenitors, based on previous evidence of expression of soxB1 genes during neurogenesis in cephalopods (Miyagi et al., 2009; Focareta and Cole, 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on previous research, with supporting citations.

claim: The lens is a specialized part of the eye for which a cluster (Cl33) was identified based on the expression of s-crystallin.
source: The lens is a specialized part of the eye for which we identified a cluster (Cl33) based on the expression of s-crystallin, an important structural component of the tissue of the lens (Tomarev and Piatigorsky, 1996).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, with supporting citation.

claim: The largest structure in the L. vulgaris nervous system are the optic lobes.
source: The largest structure in the L. vulgaris nervous system are the optic lobes.
evidence: This is a statement about the anatomy of L. vulgaris based on established knowledge.

claim: The cortex of the optic lobes is composed of an outer and inner plexiform layers and outer/inner granular layers.
source: The cortex of the optic lobes is composed of an outer and inner plexiform layers and outer/inner granular layers.
evidence: This is a statement about the anatomy of L. vulgaris based on established knowledge.

claim: The suboesophageal mass and supraoesophagal mass make up the central part of the brain and contain several different lobes.
source: The suboesophageal mass and supraoesophagal mass make up the central part of the brain and contain several different lobes.
evidence: This is a statement about the anatomy of L. vulgaris based on established knowledge.

claim: Elav-like 1, elav-like 2, amyloid beta-binding-like, and tetraspanin-8 were found to be expressed broadly across all neuronal clusters.
source: Probes were generated for the genes elav-like 1, elav-like 2, amyloid beta-binding-like, and tetraspanin-8, which were all found to be expressed broadly across all neuronal clusters (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: HCR ISH experiments confirmed the expression of elav-like 1, elav-like 2, amyloid beta-binding-like, and tetraspanin-8 throughout the nervous system of L. vulgaris.
source: HCR ISH experiments for these probes confirmed their expression throughout the nervous system of L. vulgaris, but different genes showed specificities in their expression domains and expression levels.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments.

claim: Some regions of the nervous system show co-expression of elav-like 1 and elav-like 2.
source: Some regions of the nervous system show co-expression of elav-like 1 and elav-like 2 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Both elav-like 1 and elav-like 2 are highly expressed in the optic lobes and in the neurons of the supraesophageal and suboesophageal mass.
source: Both genes are highly expressed in the optic lobes and in the neurons of the supraesophageal and suboesophageal mass.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments.

claim: Elav-like 1 is strongly expressed in the medial part of the supraesophageal mass, including neurons of the dorsal basal lobe, vertical lobe, and subvertical lobe, as well as in the optic lobes in the medial portion of the medulla.
source: However, differences in the expression patterns of elav-like 1 and elav-like 2 can be observed: elav-like 1 is strongly expressed in the medial part of the supraesophageal mass, including neurons of the dorsal basal lobe, vertical lobe, and subvertical lobe, as well as in the optic lobes in the medial portion of the medulla (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Elav-like 2 is expressed broadly in the lateral edges of the supraesophageal mass near the optic lobes and in the optic lobes.
source: Elav-like 2, on the other hand, is expressed broadly in the lateral edges of the supraesophageal mass near the optic lobes and in the optic lobes.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments.

claim: Photoreceptors of the retina do not express elav-like 1 but only elav-like 2.

claim: The different expression domains of elav-like 1 and elav-like 2 are reflected by the scRNAseq data.

claim: Differences in the expression of elav-like 1 and elav-like 2 suggest that these genes could either serve different functions specific to the neuronal subpopulations in which they are expressed or that the different expression patterns reflect distinct developmental or differentiation states.
source: Differences in the expression of these two ELAV homologs suggest that these genes could either serve different functions specific to the neuronal subpopulations in which they are expressed or that the different expression patterns reflect distinct developmental or differentiation states.

claim: Elav-like 2-expressing cells are present in the central and peripheral nervous system as well as in the lateral lips.

claim: Expression of tetraspanin-8 was observed to be present in all cells throughout the brain, providing tetraspanin-8 as a strongly expressed pan-neuronal marker.

claim: The high neural expression pattern of tetraspanin-8 suggests that it is for the function of differentiated neurons in L. vulgaris.
source: This high neural expression pattern suggests that tetraspanin-8 is for the function of differentiated neurons in L. vulgaris providing an interesting candidate for the study of neuronal function in cephalopods.

claim: The expression of amyloid beta-binding-like is observed broadly throughout the entire brain, retina, and other components of the nervous system.

claim: Expression levels of amyloid beta-binding-like differ between cells, specifically apparent in the cortex layers of the optic lobe, where the cells of the inner granular layer express lower levels compared to tetraspanin-8.

This is specifically apparent in the cortex layers of the optic lobe, where the cells of the inner granular layer express lower levels of amyloid beta-binding-like compared to tetraspanin-8 (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 3D–G).

claim: Low expression of amyloid beta-binding-like can be observed in the olfactory organ.
source: Low expression of amyloid beta-binding-like can also be observed in the olfactory organ (Figure 2—figure supplement 3F).

claim: The scRNAseq data shows that the expression of amyloid beta-binding-like protein is lower in the reflectin+ clusters (Cl20, Cl22).
source: Additionally, the scRNAseq data shows that the expression of amyloid beta-binding-like protein is lower in the reflectin+ clusters (Cl20, Cl22, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Scratch-2 was found to be highly expressed in two neuronal clusters (Cl05, Cl15) as well as in a reflectin+ cluster (Cl22).
source: The transcriptional repressor scratch-2 was found to be highly expressed in two neuronal clusters (Cl05, Cl15) as well as in a reflectin+ cluster (Cl22).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: HCR ISH expression analysis showed that scratch-2 is mostly expressed in the medulla of the optic lobes and in the supraesophageal mass in specific domains.
source: HCR ISH expression analysis showed that this gene is mostly expressed in the medulla of the optic lobes and in the supraesophageal mass in two domains lateral–ventral to the vertical lobe and anterior to the basal lobe that extends anteriorly toward the frontal lobes, as well as a stripe of cells connecting the two domains posterior to the vertical lobe (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The analysis of the expression of scratch-2 in the scRNAseq dataset highlights that the cells highly expressing this gene are distinct from neurons expressing elav-like 1, tetraspanin-8, and amyloid beta-binding-like but show more transcriptional similarities with elav-like 2-expressing cells.
source: The analysis of the expression of scratch-2 in the scRNAseq dataset highlights that the cells highly expressing this gene are distinct from neurons expressing elav-like 1, tetraspanin-8, and amyloid beta-binding-like but show more transcriptional similarities with elav-like 2-expressing cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Fmrf was shown to be expressed in some cells within the nervous system in agreement with previous anatomical studies.
source: Fmrf was shown to be expressed in some cells within the nervous system in agreement with previous anatomical studies (Wollesen et al., 2010; Wollesen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, with supporting citations.

claim: Fmrf is expressed in a region located between the dorsal basal lobe and the anterior basal lobe, surrounding the precommissural lobes, the peduncle lobe, the olfactory lobes, on the posterior part of the buccal mass and in the olfactory organ.
source: It is expressed in a region located between the dorsal basal lobe and the anterior basal lobe, surrounding the precommissural lobes, the peduncle lobe, the olfactory lobes, on the posterior part of the buccal mass and in the olfactory organ.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments.

claim: Some cells expressing fmrf are scattered throughout the optic lobes.
source: Some cells expressing fmrf are also scattered throughout the optic lobes (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: The homeobox transcription factor LIM homeobox is expressed in the vertical lobe and subvertical lobe in a domain located between the dorsal basal lobes and the frontal lobes.
source: The homeobox transcription factor LIM homeobox is expressed in the vertical lobe and subvertical lobe in a domain located between the dorsal basal lobes and the frontal lobes.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments.

claim: LIM homeobox is also expressed around the peduncle lobe and in some cells at the surface of arms and tentacles.
source: It is also expressed around the peduncle lobe and in some cells at the surface of arms and tentacles (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 6.

claim: A serotonin transporter gene is expressed in the nervous system and more particularly in the medulla of the optic lobes.
source: We identified a serotonin transporter gene that is expressed in the nervous system and more particularly in the medulla of the optic lobes.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments.

claim: Low expression of serotonin transporter can be observed throughout the nervous system and indicates that the expression of the gene in the nervous system is not specific to an anatomical structure.
source: Low expression of this gene can be observed throughout the nervous system and indicates that the expression of the gene in the nervous system is not specific to an anatomical structure (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Serotonin transporter was very highly expressed in the cornea of eyes.
source: This transporter was, however, very highly expressed in the cornea of eyes (Figure 2—figure supplement 6D–F).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6D–F.

claim: A very large proportion of neurons express glutr3.
source: The results show that a very large proportion of neurons express glutr3 but gaba-r expression is mostly restricted to the medial part of the brain and a few cells of the optic lobes (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Gaba-r expression is mostly restricted to the medial part of the brain and a few cells of the optic lobes.
source: The results show that a very large proportion of neurons express glutr3 but gaba-r expression is mostly restricted to the medial part of the brain and a few cells of the optic lobes (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Gaba-r is expressed in the region posterior to the dorsal basal lobes, between the anterior basal lobes and the frontal lobes, in the peduncle lobes and the superior buccal lobes.
source: More specifically, gaba-r is expressed in the region posterior to the dorsal basal lobes, between the anterior basal lobes and the frontal lobes, in the peduncle lobes and the superior buccal lobes (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: Gaba-r appears to be highly expressed in both neuronal and non-neural parts of the eyes but is absent from the optic lobes.
source: Gaba-r appears to also be highly expressed in both neuronal and non-neural parts of the eyes but is absent from the optic lobes.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments.

claim: Expression of glutr3 is observed all over the animals in neuronal tissues but also in epithelial and muscular tissues.
source: Expression of glutr3, on the other hand, is observed all over the animals in neuronal tissues but also in epithelial and muscular tissues.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments.

claim: The extremely broad expression pattern for glutr3 indicates that this gene is likely to have other functions unrelated to neuronal communication.
source: This extremely broad expression pattern for glutr3 indicates that this gene is likely to have other functions unrelated to neuronal communication.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on the expression pattern.

claim: The genes involved in neurotransmission normally used to differentiate neuronal populations were expressed only in few cells in the single-cell dataset.
source: The genes involved in neurotransmission normally used to differentiate neuronal populations were expressed only in few cells in the single-cell dataset (Figure 2—figure supplement 8).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 8.

claim: Two clusters (Cl02, Cl14) do not express specific transcription factors that can be associated with developmental processes but show enrichment of genes involved in cellular proliferation and protein synthesis.
source: Two clusters (Cl02, Cl14, Figure 3A) do not express specific transcription factors that can be associated with developmental processes but show enrichment of genes involved in cellular proliferation and protein synthesis (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, shown in Figure 3A and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: In Cl10 and Cl17, the transcription factor e2f3 is expressed together with other indicators of cellular proliferation, cellular growth, and nucleic acid synthesis.
source: In Cl10 and Cl17, the transcription factor e2f3 is expressed together with other indicators of cellular proliferation, cellular growth, and nucleic acid synthesis such as histone proteins (H3), ribosomal proteins (40s ribosomal protein S13, 40s ribosomal protein s19), pcna, and DNA replication licensing factors (mcm3, mcm4, mcm5).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: The role of e2f3 to promote cellular proliferation has been shown to be conserved between D. melanogaster, Caenorhabditis elegans, and mammalians.
source: The role of e2f3 to promote cellular proliferation has been shown to be conserved between D. melanogaster, Caenorhabditis elegans. and mammalians (Dynlacht et al., 1994; Attwooll et al., 2004; DeGregori and Johnson, 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Clusters expressing e2f3 and proliferation markers but lacking distinctive features of differentiated cell types may be stem cells.
source: Because these clusters highly express proliferation markers but lack any distinctive features of differentiated cell types, we propose that they may be stem cells.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the expression of specific markers.

claim: HCR ISH experiments for e2f3 showed that this gene is specifically expressed in the anatomical structure called the lateral lips.
source: To visualize the expression pattern of this gene, we performed HCR ISH experiments for e2f3. The results show that this gene is specifically expressed in the anatomical structure called the lateral lips, which have been described in O. vulgaris (Figure 3C and D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Deryckere et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 3C, Figure 3D, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, with supporting citation.

claim: The expression of e2f3 in the lateral lips suggests the presence and proliferation of stem cells or progenitors in the lateral lips of squids, consistently with the proposed neurogenic regions of O. vulgaris.
source: This suggests the presence and proliferation of stem cells or progenitors in the lateral lips of squids, consistently with the proposed neurogenic regions of O. vulgaris.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on the expression pattern and previous research.

claim: In Cl17, Cl21, and Cl26, the transcription factor achaete-scute (asc) is expressed together with proliferation markers.
source: In Cl17, Cl21, and Cl26, the transcription factor achaete-scute (asc), which has a well-studied role in the regulation of nervous system development in D. melanogaster, is expressed together with similar proliferation markers as indicated previously (Cabrera et al., 1987; Romani et al., 1987; Skeath and Carroll, 1992).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data, with supporting citations.

claim: The expression pattern of asc revealed by HCR ISH showed a strong similarity with the expression of e2f3 in the lateral lips.
source: The expression pattern revealed by HCR ISH showed a strong similarity with the expression of e2f3 in the lateral lips (Figure 3C and D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 3C, Figure 3D, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The overlapping expression of e2f3 and asc in the lateral lips suggests that neuronal progenitors and stem cells are co-located in the lateral lip where they proliferate.
source: This suggests that neuronal progenitors and stem cells are co-located in the lateral lip where they proliferate.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on the expression patterns.

claim: Frequent co-expression of asc with soxB1 in these clusters further supports their neuronal fate because of the conserved involvement of soxB1 genes in neuronal development in very distantly related species.
source: Frequent co-expression with soxB1 in these clusters further supports their neuronal fate because of the conserved involvement of soxB1 genes in neuronal development in very distantly related species such as C. elegans and mammals as well as in cephalopods (Arsic et al., 1998; Miyagi et al., 2009; Alqadah et al., 2015; Focareta and Cole, 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on the expression patterns and previous research, with supporting citations.

claim: Analysis of the expression of soxB1 revealed enriched expression in the lateral lips, similarly to e2f3 and asc.
source: We next analyzed the expression of soxB1, which revealed enriched expression in the lateral lips, similarly to e2f3 and asc.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments.

claim: The pattern of expression of soxB1 is broader than asc and is also present in most lobes of the brain.
source: Interestingly, the pattern of expression of soxB1 is broader than asc and is also present in most lobes of the brain (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The overlapping expression patterns of e2f3, asc, and soxB1 in domains associated with cephalopod neurogenesis strongly suggest that stem cells and neuronal progenitors are present in the lateral lips of L. vulgaris.
source: Together, the overlapping expression patterns of e2f3, asc, and soxB1 in domains associated with cephalopod neurogenesis strongly suggest that stem cells and neuronal progenitors are present the lateral lips of L. vulgaris, suggesting that these cells are likely migrating to the nervous system at later differentiation stages.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on the expression patterns.

claim: Stem cells and neuronal progenitors in the lateral lips are likely migrating to the nervous system at later differentiation stages.
source: Together, the overlapping expression patterns of e2f3, asc, and soxB1 in domains associated with cephalopod neurogenesis strongly suggest that stem cells and neuronal progenitors are present the lateral lips of L. vulgaris, suggesting that these cells are likely migrating to the nervous system at later differentiation stages.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the expression patterns.

claim: In agreement with a pro-neural function, cells expressing e2f3, asc, and soxB1 do not yet express markers of terminally differentiated neurons.
source: In agreement with a pro-neural function, these cells do not yet express markers of terminally differentiated neurons.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: SoxB1 was previously shown to be expressed throughout late embryogenesis in the developing eye of D. pealeii.
source: It was previously shown that soxB1 is expressed throughout late embryogenesis in the developing eye of D. pealeii (Napoli et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Comparable expression of soxB1 was found in the developing eye in L. vulgaris pre-hatchling.
source: We indeed found comparable expression of soxB1 in the developing eye in L. vulgaris pre-hatchling and further detected expression in the developing olfactory organ, suggesting a broader role of soxB1 in sensory organ development or function (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Expression of soxB1 was detected in the developing olfactory organ, suggesting a broader role of soxB1 in sensory organ development or function.
source: We indeed found comparable expression of soxB1 in the developing eye in L. vulgaris pre-hatchling and further detected expression in the developing olfactory organ, suggesting a broader role of soxB1 in sensory organ development or function (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on the expression pattern, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Cl16, Cl19, and Cl30 are characterized by the expression of the forkhead box transcription factor foxD1.
source: Cl16, Cl19, and Cl30 are characterized by the expression of the forkhead box transcription factor foxD1.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: FoxD genes have been documented to be expressed in the nervous systems of Mus musculus, Xenopus laevi, C. elegans, and D. melanogaster and to play a role in the development of neuronal cell types although not exclusively.
source: FoxD genes have been documented to be expressed in the nervous systems of Mus musculus, Xenopus laevi, C. elegans, and D. melanogaster and to play a role in the development of neuronal cell types although not exclusively (Herrera et al., 2004; Polevoy et al., 2017; Newman et al., 2018; Janssen et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: HCR ISH assessment of the expression of foxD1 showed that these cells are strongly expressed in the cortex of the optic lobes and in the medial basal and anterior basal lobes.
source: HCR ISH assessment of the expression of foxD1 showed that these cells are strongly expressed in the cortex of the optic lobes and in the medial basal and anterior basal lobes (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The expression of foxD1 is very strong in the cortex of the optic lobes and in the medial and anterior basal lobes but is also sparsely located in the medulla.
source: The expression of foxD1 is very strong in the cortex of the optic lobes and in the medial and anterior basal lobes but is also sparsely located in the medulla (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The expression pattern of foxD1 indicated that these cell types are present in the nervous system and could therefore be types of neurons or neuronal progenitors.
source: The expression pattern of foxD1 indicated that these cell types are present in the nervous system and could therefore be types of neurons or neuronal progenitors.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on the expression pattern.

claim: Cl30 also expressed a GATA zinc finger transcription factor (gata-2) together with some markers typically associated with blood cells (hemocyte protein, immunoglobulin, soma-ferritin, apolipophorin).
source: Cl30 also expressed a GATA zinc finger transcription factor (gata-2) together with some markers typically associated with blood cells (hemocyte protein, immunoglobulin, soma-ferritin, apolipophorin).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: The expression pattern of gata-2 is very similar to foxD1 and is also strongly expressed in the cortex of the optic lobes.
source: The expression pattern of gata-2 is very similar to foxD1 and is also strongly expressed in the cortex of the optic lobes (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Gata-2 expression can also be found at the surface of the arms and in the suckers.
source: Gata-2 expression can also be found at the surface of the arms and in the suckers.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments.

claim: The HCR ISH experiments showed that the expression of e2f3 and asc is limited to the proliferating cells located in the lateral lips, whereas the expression of foxD1 and gata-2 is not found in the lateral lips but inside nervous tissue.
source: The HCR ISH experiments with these different genes showed that the expression of e2f3 and asc is limited to the proliferating cells located in the lateral lips, whereas the expression of foxD1 and gata-2 is not found in the lateral lips but inside nervous tissue.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments.

claim: The expression pattern of soxB1 revealed that it is present both in the lateral lips and the nervous tissue of the optic lobes.
source: The expression pattern of soxB1 revealed that it is present both in the lateral lips and the nervous tissue of the optic lobes (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Trajectory analysis was performed on a subset of cells including stem cell clusters, neuronal clusters, foxD+ clusters, and asc+ clusters.
source: To assess the possible developmental lineages that could link these different clusters together, we performed trajectory analysis on a subset of cells. We selected all the cells from the stem cell clusters (Cl02, Cl10, Cl14, Cl17), the neuronal clusters including photoreceptors and presumed sensory cells (Cl05, Cl07, Cl11, Cl13, Cl27, Cl32), the foxD+ clusters (Cl16, Cl19, Cl30), and the asc+ clusters (Cl21, Cl26).
evidence: This describes the computational analysis approach.

claim: Trajectory analysis using Monocle3 was performed on the selected cells.
source: These cells were used for subclustering and subsequent trajectory analysis using Monocle3 (Trapnell et al., 2014; Qiu et al., 2017b; Qiu et al., 2017a).
evidence: This describes the computational analysis approach.

claim: The e2f3 expressing cluster was selected as a starting point for the trajectories.
source: We selected the e2f3 expressing cluster as a starting point for the trajectories and the results indicated that following the proliferative stage where cells express e2F3 and asc, cell trajectories go through a stage where foxD1 and gata-2 are strongly expressed (Figure 3E).
evidence: This describes the computational analysis approach, shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Following the proliferative stage where cells express e2F3 and asc, cell trajectories go through a stage where foxD1 and gata-2 are strongly expressed.
source: We selected the e2f3 expressing cluster as a starting point for the trajectories and the results indicated that following the proliferative stage where cells express e2F3 and asc, cell trajectories go through a stage where foxD1 and gata-2 are strongly expressed (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from the trajectory analysis, shown in Figure 3E.

claim: After the foxD1 and gata-2 expressing stage, there is increased expression of the markers of differentiated neurons amyloid beta-binding-like.
source: After this stage, we see increased expression of the markers of differentiated neurons amyloid beta-binding-like (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from the trajectory analysis, shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The expression of soxB1 along the trajectory axis appears to be present in the early stages as well as in the differentiated neurons, consistently with the expression patterns previously observed by HCR ISH.
source: The expression of soxB1 along the trajectory axis appears to be present in the early stages as well as in the differentiated neurons, consistently with the expression patterns previously observed by HCR ISH (Figure 3C and E).
evidence: This is a finding from the trajectory analysis, shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3E.

claim: The expression level of soxB1 is very low in the foxD1-expressing stage.
source: The expression level of soxB1 is, however, very low in the foxD1-expressing stage.
evidence: This is a finding from the trajectory analysis.

claim: The proliferation markers pcna and histone H3 and the transcription factor elf-2 show similar expression as e2f3 and asc in the early stages of differentiation.
source: Additional markers could be plotted along the trajectory axis: the proliferation markers pcna and histone H3 and the transcription factor elf-2 show similar expression as e2f3 and asc in the early stages of differentiation (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the trajectory analysis, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The hypothetical intermediate stage characterized by the expression of foxD1 and gata-2 could be correlated with the expression of the transcription factors ets4 and hes-4 as well as chemotrypsin.
source: The hypothetical intermediate stage characterized by the expression of foxD1 and gata-2 could also be correlated with the expression of the transcription factors ets4 and hes-4 as well as chemotrypsin (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the trajectory analysis, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Elav-like 1, elav-like 2, and synaptogyrin-1 are highly expressed in the differentiated neurons, and although they are present across all clusters, the average expression increases along the differentiation axis.
source: Elav-like 1, elav-like 2, and synaptogyrin-1 are highly expressed in the differentiated, and although they are present across all clusters, the average expression increases along the differentiation axis (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the trajectory analysis, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Trajectory inference analysis using slingshot was performed to support the results shown by monocle 3.
source: To support the results shown by the monocle 3 trajectory inference, we performed a similar analysis with slingshot (Street et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the computational analysis approach.

claim: The results obtained with slingshot were very similar to those obtained with monocle and showed a trajectory that supports foxD1+ cells as a possible intermediate stage between the proliferative stage and the differentiated neurons.
source: The results obtained with slingshot were very similar to those obtained with monocle and showed a trajectory that supports foxD1+ cells as a possible intermediate stage between the proliferative stage where e2f3 and asc are expressed and the differentiated neurons expressing amyloid beta-binding-like and higher levels of elav-like 1 and elav-like 2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the trajectory analysis, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: The calculation of trajectories using monocle and slingshot provides insights into the developmental relationship between different identified cell types and provides new hypotheses for the study of neurogenesis of cephalopods.
source: The calculation of trajectories using these two separate methods provides insights into the developmental relationship between these different identified cell types and provides new hypotheses for the study of neurogenesis of cephalopods.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the trajectory analysis results.

claim: Vision is a crucial sense for various behaviors of the squids as it is needed for navigating efficiently in open waters in the wild.
source: Vision is a crucial sense for various behaviors of the squids as it is needed for navigating efficiently in open waters in the wild.
evidence: This is a statement about squid behavior based on established knowledge.

claim: The eyes of squids are very large and the optic lobes take up a significant part of the overall volume of the brain.
source: The eyes of squids are very large and the optic lobes, where visual information is processed and integrated, take up a significant part of the overall volume of the brain.
evidence: This is a statement about squid anatomy based on established knowledge.

claim: The phototransduction cascade that allows light stimuli to be transformed into an electrical signal in the neurons is well conserved among cephalopods.
source: The phototransduction cascade that allows light stimuli to be transformed into an electrical signal in the neurons is well conserved among cephalopods, and we were able to clearly identify photoreceptors in the scRNAseq data (Davies et al., 1996; Monk et al., 1996; Arendt, 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Photoreceptors were clearly identified in the scRNAseq data.
source: The phototransduction cascade that allows light stimuli to be transformed into an electrical signal in the neurons is well conserved among cephalopods, and we were able to clearly identify photoreceptors in the scRNAseq data (Davies et al., 1996; Monk et al., 1996; Arendt, 2003).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: Many important components of the phototransduction cascade are highly expressed in Cl32 such as trp-like, retinochrome, arrestin, phospholipase C, and rhodopsin.
source: Many important components of the phototransduction cascade are highly expressed in Cl32 such as trp-like, retinochrome, arrestin, phospholipase C, and rhodopsin.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on the analysis of single-cell transcriptomics data.

claim: HCR ISH probes for trp-like and rhodopsin showed striking specificity and are expressed in the photoreceptors of the retina.
source: To verify the expression of members of the phototransduction cascade in the photoreceptors, HCR ISH probes for trp-like and rhodopsin were selected and tested. Both genes showed striking specificity and are expressed in the photoreceptors of the retina (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on HCR ISH experiments, shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The olfactory organs of L. vulgaris are located on the ventral surface of the head.
source: The olfactory organs of L. vulgaris are located on the ventral surface of the head (see Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a statement about the anatomy of L. vulgaris, shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The genes involved in the function of the olfactory organs remain unknown and thus no cell type-specific markers were readily available to identify chemosensory cells of the olfactory organ.
